# Tire Pressure Guidelines

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

## Summary

[Partial] [Unverified value] Check door jamb sticker to verify if stock tires are marked 'P' rated or 'LT', then run LTs at 35 PSI. [t212]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Check the door jamb sticker for the factory-recommended tire pressure.
2. [Partial] Verify if the stock tires are marked as 'P' rated or 'LT' (Light Truck) to understand load capacity needs.

_Procedure reported by [t212]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Unverified value] Run Light Truck (LT) tires at 35 PSI for a balance of safety, braking ability, and even tread wear. [t212]
- [Unverified value] Note that 'P' rated stock sizes typically operate best at 35 PSI to maximize the contact patch across the entire width. [t212]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] [Unverified value] Filling LT tires to their absolute maximum rating (e.g., 80 PSI) for normal driving, which risks overheating and blowouts as air expands with heat. [t212]
- [Partial] Ignoring that higher pressures reduce the rolling contact patch, increasing center tread wear. [t212]
